gate.description: The gate name from .fluxpoint-gates.json that was run. A name, not a command: the command is whatever the committed manifest declares, so a node cannot widen what it claims to have run.

exit.description: The exit code the gate produced. Still typed by the node — what makes it worth anything is that record-run.py refuses it unless the attest log, written by a hook the agent does not mediate, agrees.

attestId.description: The row in .claude/fluxpoint/attest.jsonl this claim cites. Minted when the command ran by a witness the agent does not mediate: the PostToolUse hook, attest.py --run for a gate too long for one tool call, or attest.py --ci from the forge's own statuses. A claim citing an id that does not exist, or one whose recorded exit differs, is TAMPERED-EXECUTION; a row minted before this run launched, on another commit, or already backing another node is STALE.

sha.description: The commit the gate judged. Required when citing prove:ci: record-run.py checks it against the commit the forge named in the cited row, and the merge the gate guards should pin it (gh pr merge --match-head-commit).

logSha256.description: Hash of the run's combined output, as the hook recorded it. Lets a later reader bind a quoted log to the execution it came from.
